item.description: Much of what is now Minnesota formed part of the vast French holding of Louisiana, which the United States purchased in 1803. After several territorial reorganizations, the Minnesota Territory was admitted to the Union as the 32nd state in 1858.

item.title: About Minnesota / mn.gov // Minnesota's State Portal
item.description: Minnesota, is in the north central United States. Near the geographic center of North America, it is bordered on the north by the Canadian provinces of Manitoba and Ontario, on the west by North Dakota and South Dakota, on the south by Iowa, and on the east by Wisconsin and Lake Superior.

item.title: Minnesota Maps & Facts - World Atlas
item.description: Minnesota, a state in the upper Midwest of the United States, borders Canada to the north, Lake Superior and Wisconsin to the northeast, Iowa to the south, and South Dakota and North Dakota to the west.

item.title: Minnesota: Outdoor Beauty, Cultured Fun - Visit The USA
item.description: Today, Minnesota is still known for its breathtaking scenery — majestic forests, vast prairielands and sparkling waterways — alongside vibrant arts and culture.

item.title: Geography of Minnesota - Wikipedia
item.description: The U.S. state of Minnesota is the northernmost state outside Alaska; its isolated Northwest Angle in Lake of the Woods is the only part of the 48 contiguous states lying north of the 49th parallel north. Minnesota is in the U.S. region known as the Upper Midwest in interior North America.

item.title: Minnesota | Flag, Minneapolis, Governor, Map, Cities, & Facts | Britannica
item.description: Minnesota, constituent state of the United States of America. It became the 32nd state of the union on May 11, 1858. A small extension of the northern boundary makes Minnesota the most northerly of the 48 conterminous U.S. states.

item.title: THE 15 BEST Things to Do in Minnesota (2026) - Tripadvisor
item.description: According to forum posts, travelers looking for scenic routes in Minnesota have several options.
